content.title: 2023 Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation
content.figure: Treatment Algorithm for Pharmacological Conversion of AF to Sinus Rhythm

af_outside_hospital.description: AF occurring outside the hospital in patients with normal LV function ("pill-in-the-pocket")

key_points: Amiodarone requires several hours for efficacy.
Ibutilide is generally effective within 30 to 90 minutes.
Amiodarone and Ibutilide may cause QT interval prolongation and torsades de pointes.
Procainamide can be considered for selected patients.

studies.finding: Relative risks of sinus rhythm with intravenous amiodarone at 6 to 8 hours and 24 hours were 1.23 (P=0.022) and 1.44 (P<0.001).
Pharmacological cardioversion of AF with intravenous amiodarone requires 8 to 12 hours compared to shorter response time with ibutilide.
Single oral doses of flecainide and propafenone are effective with 4-hour conversion rates.
